prepare.what:
Four builders can now work on Tabs, DropdownMenu, Dialog and Input at the same time, each building and testing a private copy of the gallery, and Button passes again under the changed spec. The Button run printed "1 components, 18 examples, 637 checks, 634 passed, 0 failed, 3 not reached or not run, 0 not proven". All four tools' --self-test exit 0, and build-components builds all five specs.

Generator (v2/tools/build-components.mjs):
- **Contracts:** in a compound spec a key part.prop goes into <Name><Part>Props under the name after the dot (trigger.value becomes value in TabsTriggerProps), and its enum union is named <Name><Part><Prop> (TabsListBehavior). Plain keys go into <Name>Props. A single-piece spec (no dotted key) puts every prop in <Name>Props. <NAME>_DEFAULTS and <NAME>_REFLECTS keep the spec's own keys (dotted ones included), grouped by exported component. A default of null is left out of DEFAULTS and listed in a comment as "unset unless given".
- **Parts whose element is null:** they get no CSS, and <NAME>_SLOTS marks them "renders nothing". A style rule, a state, or a prop condition that names one is a build error.
- **Flat specificity:** every condition, precedence exclusion and ancestor part is wrapped in :where(). I checked this against the files on disk: 0 of 46 / 12 / 37 / 31 / 29 selectors in button / dialog / dropdown-menu / input / tabs .css are anything but the bare part selector.
- **index.ts:** generated inside buildAll from the folders that hold <slug>.tsx, using the two lines from the brief.
- **Reference pages:** no length limit; one row per token, every style rule listed, and descriptions and notes kept.
- **Filtered build:** `build-components.mjs <slug>` now always builds every spec. It writes only that component's own files, plus shared files that keep every component. I checked this with `tabs`: styles.css, index.ts and state-map.md came out byte-identical, and button.css was not touched.
- **Self-test:** went from 13 to 27 planted checks, with expected strings updated for the new selectors. It catches the faults it should: removing the :where() wrapping made 6 checks fail.

Gallery and runner:
- **build-gallery.mjs:** new options `--dist <dir>` and `--component <slug>[,<slug>]`. A non-default dist gets its own registry inside it, so builders never write the same file.
- **test-components.mjs:**
  - `--dist <dir>` serves that folder as its own root and builds nothing; a missing bundle is an error.
  - `--report <file>` writes the JSON report even on a filtered run.
  - `type:<id>` passes only when `npx --no-install tsc -p ds-components/tsconfig.json` exits 0 (run once per run) and a line of hand-written source holds both "@ts-expect-error" and the id as a whole word. Otherwise it is a new status, "not proven", which is counted in the summary line.
  - The anatomy check skips parts whose element is null, and a state check's colour lookup falls back to searching the whole page, which is what portalled parts need.
  - The self-test went to 29 expectations, including 5 type: cases and the missing-bundle case.

Lint (lint-components.mjs):
- Parts whose element is null need not appear in the source, and a data-slot that names one is an error. The fixture now has such a part, and the clean baseline stays at 0 errors.
- The tsconfig it writes now excludes gallery/dist and gallery/dist-*.
- Its in-memory rebuild reads the component folders of the tree being linted.

Icons: 25 added. These are the names the four specs' examples use (truck, store, share, archive, external-link, clipboard, folder, location, pencil, copy, more-horizontal, chevron-up), plus the rest of the brief's list.

Button:
- button.tsx: imports only ButtonProps from the contract, sets data-disabled when disabled (never while loading), and the @ts-expect-error line now names button-icon-only-needs-label.
- button.extensions.css: the spinner uses var(--duration-spin).
- button.tests.mjs: new test button-loading-keeps-look, plus data-disabled assertions in the disabled and loading tests.
- button.examples.tsx: unchanged, because nothing in the spec change needed it.

Requirements: 14 of 14 test: requirements passed, type:button-icon-only-needs-label passed and axe:button-name passed. 3 were not run: 1 lint: and 2 manual:.

Proof the new checks fail when they should: I made one temporary edit (data-disabled while loading, and the id removed from the directive line), ran it through `--dist`, then restored the file. button-loading-keeps-look and button-loading-stays-focusable failed, and the type requirement reported "not proven".

Ordering, checked in a real browser in both themes:
- A ghost button that is disabled stays transparent.
- A disabled primary button equals --color-interactive-primary-disabled: rgb(240, 241, 242) in light, rgb(43, 44, 47) in dark.
- A disabled button that is hovered keeps that fill.
- The Button spec has no variant rule and size rule that set the same property. That case is proven by a planted self-test rule, and in the browser by a similar pair: the icon-only rule written after the small-size rule wins (inline padding 0 px against 12 px).

COMPONENT-PATTERN.md now covers:
- who may write which file, and that only the generator writes index.ts, <slug>.css and <slug>.contract.ts (builders do not edit icons.tsx either);
- the build and test commands for a builder's own dist folder;
- how parts are exported and typed from the split contract, with a TabsList snippet that I compiled with tsc (exit 0);
- that Radix's own props pass through and the spec's props sit on top;
- never passing a null default to Radix;
- how tests find portalled parts anywhere on the page by data-slot;
- how examples expose state to tests through window.__<slug>Events;
- how flat specificity works, and the shared tsc hazard described under the remaining problems.

spec_problems: The index.ts form in the brief fails tsc on its own. Each <slug>.tsx exports <Name>Props (the pattern requires it) and so does its contract, so `export *` plus `export type *` gives TS2308, which I reproduced in a scratch check. The generator keeps both lines and adds `export type { ButtonProps } from './button/button';` for every name both files export, so the component's type wins. tsc then exits 0.

Because the brief requires `export type *` for the contract, BUTTON_DEFAULTS, BUTTON_SLOTS, BUTTON_STATES and BUTTON_REFLECTS are now type-only exports from the package entry. The old hand-written index exported them as values. Nothing in the repo imported them from the index (checked with grep). The pattern doc tells builders to import the values from ./<slug>.contract.

'As today' in item 1a was not accurate for single-piece specs. The old generator emitted per-part interfaces (ButtonIconStartProps, ButtonIconEndProps, ButtonLabelProps). Following the plain reading, every prop now goes into <Name>Props and those interfaces are gone. button.tsx was updated to match.

Flat specificity can change which rule wins in the four compound specs wherever the old specificity disagreed with spec order. This is intended: it now matches the runner's in-order colour prediction. Builders must treat spec order as the truth.

The Button spec has no variant rule and size rule that set the same property, so the 'size after variant wins' case cannot be shown from the Button stylesheet itself. It is proven by a planted rule pair in the self-test, and in the browser by the icon-only-after-small pair (inline padding 0 px against 12 px).

components.what:
I built Input from ds-components/specs/input.spec.json, in ds-components/src/input/. It is one component around the native input, exported as Input.
- Props are typed from the generated contract. Native input attributes and ref pass through to the <input>, without the native "size" and "prefix". className goes on the root. The caller's own aria-describedby is added after the component's ids.
- Two unions enforce the type rules: either label or ariaLabel is required, and invalid: true needs an errorMessage that is not null, undefined or a boolean. Each union is proved by a // @ts-expect-error line naming its requirement id.
- Ids come from React.useId when no id is given. The description and error ids are <id>-description and <id>-error.
- The error message, data-invalid and aria-invalid all appear only while invalid is true and an error message is given. aria-describedby lists the error id first, then the description id, and only ids of parts that are on the page.
- The word Required sits in the label with aria-hidden, next to the native required attribute. The prefix, suffix and error icon also carry aria-hidden. The error icon is an inline SVG drawn in the component, because the gallery icons are not shipped.
- Pressing the control outside the input moves focus to the input. The handler is onMouseDown with preventDefault.
- The component warns once in development for a missing name and for invalid without a message.
- input.extensions.css carries the layout the spec lists under notCarried: the root is a column, the control is a row centred vertically, the input takes the width left over and may shrink, the prefix and suffix keep their size, and the error message is a row with the icon first. It also resets margins on the p elements and sizes an icon given as prefix or suffix to --size-icon-md.
- input.examples.tsx has all 19 spec examples. input.tests.mjs has all 20 test:<id> requirements, each a real browser test.
- Results: 25 of 26 requirements the runner checks pass. input-focus-visible fails because of a generator bug: Chromium draws its own focus ring inside the control's ring. Lint and types show no error in the input files, and the bundle is within the size limits.
- 136 runner checks fail. All but one are tool limits or spec problems, listed under failing checks. The one real fault is the doubled focus ring.

components.what:
I built Tabs from ds-components/specs/tabs.spec.json. It wraps @radix-ui/react-tabs and exports Tabs, TabsList, TabsTrigger and TabsContent.

**Results.** All 34 named requirement tests pass. tsc exits 0, and lint shows no errors in the tabs files. The runner still shows 90 failures for tabs. Every one is a runner or spec gap, not a fault in the component; they are listed with their numbers in failing_or_not_run.

**Tabs (root).**
- Renders a div with data-slot="tabs" and reflects data-variant and data-size.
- Spreads dir, value and defaultValue only when they are given.
- Its props type requires value or defaultValue.

**TabsList.**
- Its props type requires ariaLabel or ariaLabelledby. A `@ts-expect-error tabs-list-needs-name` line proves it: making ariaLabel optional made tsc fail with TS2578.
- When it first renders, it scrolls the selected tab into view inside the list, and again once fonts have loaded. It uses scrollBy on the list only, never scrollIntoView, so the page does not move.

**TabsTrigger.**
- Renders, in order: iconStart (aria-hidden), the label, iconEnd (aria-hidden), and an indicator span (aria-hidden) in every tab.
- On focus it scrolls the tab fully into view inside the list, keeping the list's padding around it so the focus ring is not cut off.

**Two fixes the tests forced:**
1. **Radix called onValueChange twice per press in controlled mode** (once from the focus the press gives, once from the press). tabs-one-selected caught it: the log read ["details","details"]. Tabs now drops a repeat of the same value within the same task.
2. **In forced colours every tab showed a line.** Chromium repaints the transparent indicator borders as solid 2 px rgb(0,0,0). The extensions stylesheet now hides unselected indicators, and all pill indicators, in forced colours.

**Two things you should know about:**
- **`data-label` on the label part.** I added this attribute so the stylesheet can reserve the width of the bold selected label: a hidden ::after copy with `content: attr(data-label) / ""`. It is not the reflection of a spec prop, which the settled convention ties data attributes to. It reserves width only when the label is plain text. Chromium's accessibility tree confirms each tab's name is exactly its label.
- **The extensions stylesheet sets the indicator's one-edge border style and width (longhands only),** because the spec hands that to it. state:selected confirms the colour still comes from the border/brand token.

**Tests catch faults.** I broke the component on purpose and each named test failed, then restored the files:
- No overflow on the list: 5 tests failed.
- No reserved width: tabs-no-width-shift failed.
- No scroll on first render: tabs-selected-in-view-on-mount failed.
- No scroll on focus: tabs-focused-tab-in-view and tabs-focus-visible failed.
- Indicator border written as a shorthand: state:selected and tabs-selected-not-colour-alone failed.

Item focus ring: the spec says 'No ring on items: the highlight is the focus indicator', but its base item rule sets no outline. Chromium therefore draws its default 'outline auto 1px' ring on the keyboard-highlighted item, as seen in the pictures. The pattern forbids outline in the extensions stylesheet, so the base item rules need outline-style none outside forced colours. components.what:
Built Dialog end to end from ds-components/specs/dialog.spec.json on @radix-ui/react-dialog 1.3.1. dialog.tsx exports the 11 parts: Dialog, DialogTrigger, DialogPortal, DialogOverlay, DialogContent, DialogHeader, DialogTitle, DialogDescription, DialogBody, DialogFooter and DialogClose. As the spec says, the content sits inside the overlay. The modal prop is fixed to true and not exposed. On top of Radix, the adapter adds:
- aria-modal="true" on the content.
- A development console.warn when a DialogContent mounts without a DialogTitle or with an empty one.
- content.dismissible=false, which blocks Escape and the outside press.
- content.initialFocus: control focuses the first tabbable control that is not a link and not the body; title focuses the title, which then has tabindex -1. Without a control, focus goes to the content.
- Focus return for a dialog that has no trigger: the element that had focus on open is recorded inside onOpenAutoFocus and refocused on close. Triggers register through a Souvenir context, so Radix still returns focus to the trigger when there is one.
- The body joins the Tab order only while it scrolls, so it can be scrolled with the keyboard.
